content: I can see a cross-section of a corn ear with white mold/mycelium in the center cob area and some discolored kernels with pinkish tones. This looks like an ear rot. Let me compare with reference images for the ear rot candidates.

Based on my analysis:

**Test image observations:**
- Cross-section view from the butt end of a corn ear
- White mycelium/mold growing in the cob center and between kernels
- Kernels appear grayish-brown and discolored
- No distinct pink/red coloring (rules out Gibberella)
- No green powdery mold (rules out Aspergillus/Trichoderma)
- Mold appears to originate from the base

**Key distinguishing features:**
- **Diplodia ear rot**: White mold starting from the base, grayish-brown discoloration — matches well
- **Fusarium**: White-pink cottony mold on scattered kernels with starburst pattern — doesn't match the uniform base-originating pattern
- **Gibberella**: Pink-red mold from the tip — no pink/red seen here

The white mycelium growing from the base with grayish-brown kernel discoloration is the hallmark of Diplodia ear rot.
